breakfast.name: Dal Bhat (Lentils and Rice)
instructions: Cook rice
Cook lentils with turmeric, cumin
Make tadka: fry garlic, ginger, cumin in ghee
Pour tadka into dal
Serve with rice and tarkari
breakfast.description: Nepal's national meal — eaten twice daily, at breakfast and dinner.

breakfast.name: Sel Roti (Rice Doughnuts)
instructions: Blend rice flour with banana, sugar, cardamom
Make thick batter
Pour ring shapes into hot oil
Fry until golden and crispy
breakfast.description: Ring-shaped rice doughnuts — made during festivals.

breakfast.name: Sel Roti (Ring-Shaped Fried Rice Bread)
ingredients: Banana (very ripe — for sweetness and binding)
instructions: Sel roti is Nepal's traditional festive fried bread — a ring-shaped crispy sweet treat
Made especially for Tihar (Diwali equivalent) and Dashain (the most important Nepali festival)
Mix rice flour with mashed banana, sugar, cardamom, fennel
The banana acts as both sweetener and binder
Adjust with water to a thick, pourable batter
Deep fry: pour the batter through a hole in a plastic bag or funnel in a circle
The circle technique: pour in a ring shape in the hot oil
Fry until golden-brown — crispy outside, slightly chewy inside
The batter must be exactly right — too thin makes it fragile, too thick means dense
A good sel roti: golden, evenly crispy, not too oily
Made by women in the family before festivals — the smell of frying sel roti signals celebration
breakfast.description: Nepal's festive ring bread — rice flour and ripe banana batter poured in circles into hot oil, forming crispy golden rings. Made before Dashain and Tihar (Nepal's two most important festivals); the smell of frying sel roti in the neighborhood signals the festival has begun. The banana provides natural sweetness and binding. The ring shape requires skill — the batter must be the right thickness.

breakfast.name: Yomari (Steamed Rice Dumpling)
ingredients: Filling: chaku (molasses candy + sesame) OR khuwa (milk fudge)
instructions: Yomari is the traditional Newar food of the Kathmandu Valley
Made specifically for the Yomari Punhi festival (December, full moon after rice harvest)
The shape: a fish or elongated teardrop — symbolic
Rice flour dough: hot water kneaded into a pliable, smooth dough
Fill each piece with chaku (raw sugar and sesame paste) or khuwa (reduced milk sweet)
Pinch the ends shut — the shape must hold during steaming
Steam 15-20 minutes
Yomari is only available at Yomari Punhi — makes it precious
The Newar (indigenous people of Kathmandu Valley) are the original inhabitants of the valley
Their food culture is distinct from hill Nepali — more ritualized, more Buddhist/Hindu intertwined
Children receive yomari as a reward during the festival — the number represents their age
breakfast.description: The Newar people's festival dumpling — rice flour dough shaped into elongated teardrops, filled with chaku (raw sugar and sesame) or khuwa (milk fudge), and steamed. Made only for Yomari Punhi (the full moon festival after the rice harvest, December). The Newar are Kathmandu Valley's indigenous people; their food culture is distinct from hill Nepali. Children receive yomari equal to their age.

lunch.name: Momos (Nepali Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: minced buffalo or chicken, onion, cilantro, ginger, garlic, cumin, chili
instructions: Make dough, rest
Mix filling
Roll wrappers, fill
Pleat and pinch closed
Steam 15 min
Serve with spicy tomato achar
lunch.description: Nepal's beloved dumplings — steamed and served with spicy tomato pickle.

lunch.name: Thukpa (Noodle Soup)
instructions: Sauté garlic, ginger, tomato
Add broth, bring to boil
Add noodles and protein
Cook until done
Top with green onion and chili

lunch.name: Thukpa (Tibetan Noodle Soup)
instructions: Thukpa comes from Tibet — brought to Nepal by the Tibetan diaspora and Himalayan communities
It's the warming soup of Nepal's high-altitude communities — the mountain food
Fry onion, garlic, ginger until fragrant
Add tomatoes — cook down until soft
Add spices: turmeric, cumin, coriander, chili
Add chicken or vegetables, stock or water
Add noodles — they cook in the soup (thick noodles work best)
Add spinach or cabbage in the last minutes
Top with cilantro
Thukpa is eaten across Nepal's mountain regions — Sherpa communities, Tibetan refugees, and Himalayan trekkers
The warming, filling, noodle-heavy soup is exactly what the altitude and cold demand
Trekkers on the Everest Base Camp trail eat thukpa as a warming staple
lunch.description: Nepal's mountain noodle soup — Tibetan in origin, brought to Nepal by Himalayan and Tibetan communities, now eaten across Nepal's high-altitude regions. Thick noodles in a spiced tomato-ginger broth with chicken or vegetables. Warming, filling, and exactly right for altitude. Sherpa communities, Tibetan refugees, and Everest trekkers all eat thukpa as the mountain warming dish.

lunch.name: Aloo Tama (Potato and Bamboo Shoot Curry)
ingredients: Tama (fermented bamboo shoots — the essential Nepali ingredient)
Mustard oil (the cooking oil of Nepal)
Turmeric, cumin, fenugreek, timur pepper (Nepali Sichuan pepper)
instructions: Tama (fermented bamboo shoots) is one of Nepal's most distinctive ingredients
The fermentation gives a unique sour, slightly funky flavor — no substitute
It's a traditional Newar dish — aloo tama ko jhol
Fry mustard oil with fenugreek and dried chili until the mustard oil loses its raw flavor
Add garlic, ginger, timur pepper — timur is the Nepali Sichuan pepper (related but different)
Add potato and fermented bamboo shoot — the bamboo shoot's sourness is the flavor base
Add black-eyed peas, water
Simmer until potato is cooked through
The mustard oil + fenugreek + timur combination is distinctly Nepali — found nowhere else
Aloo tama is a uniquely Nepali flavor profile — the fermented bamboo is irreplaceable
Eaten with rice — the sour stew with plain rice is the balance
lunch.description: Nepal's distinctively Nepali curry — fermented bamboo shoots (tama, sour and funky from fermentation) with potato and beans in a mustard oil base with fenugreek and timur (Nepali Sichuan pepper). The fermented bamboo shoot's sourness is irreplaceable — this is one of those dishes where a key ingredient is genuinely Nepali-specific. The mustard oil-fenugreek-timur base is found nowhere else.

dinner.name: Newari Khaja Set
instructions: Grill and spice meat for choila
Cook beans
Sauté spinach
Make potato dish
Make pickle
Arrange all on plate with beaten rice
dinner.description: Newar feast plate — an array of small dishes with beaten rice.

dinner.name: Sukuti (Dried Meat)
instructions: Slice meat thin, rub with spices
Dry in sun 2-3 days
When ready, fry in oil until crispy
Serve as side dish
dinner.description: Dried and fried spiced buffalo meat.

dinner.name: Gundruk (Fermented Greens) Soup
ingredients: Gundruk (dried fermented greens — mustard leaves, radish leaves, or cauliflower leaves)
instructions: Gundruk is Nepal's national fermented vegetable — UNESCO recently acknowledged its cultural importance
Made by allowing wilted vegetable leaves to ferment in a warm, dark place for 5-7 days
Then dried in the sun — can be stored for years
The fermentation is natural lactic acid — creates a sour, complex flavor
Reconstitute gundruk in water — it softens and releases flavor
Fry onion and garlic in mustard oil
Add tomato, turmeric, chili
Add reconstituted gundruk and its soaking liquid
The soaking liquid has flavor — use it all
Simmer 15 minutes
Gundruk ko jhol is eaten daily in rural Nepal
It's the village vegetable preservation — making leaves keep through winter
The sour-funky flavor of gundruk is the flavor of Nepali home cooking
dinner.description: Nepal's national fermented vegetable — mustard or radish leaves wilted, fermented naturally for a week, then sun-dried until they keep for years. Gundruk is simmered into a sour, savory soup in mustard oil with tomato and turmeric. The fermentation creates a complex sourness that defines Nepali village cooking. Gundruk was recently acknowledged by UNESCO for its cultural significance in Nepali food heritage.

dinner.name: Kwati (Nine-Bean Soup)
ingredients: Nine types of sprouted beans and lentils: green mung, black mung, soybean, black-eyed pea, chickpea, field pea, garden pea, broad bean, rice bean
instructions: Kwati is a traditional Newari soup eaten during Janai Purnima (full moon of Shrawan — August)
The nine beans represent the nine planets (navagraha) in Hindu-Buddhist cosmology
All beans are sprouted first — this takes 2-3 days but improves nutrition and digestibility
Sprouting: soak overnight, drain, keep moist — the sprouts emerge in 1-2 days
Fry onion, garlic, ginger in mustard oil
Add spices — timur pepper is important
Add the sprouted beans with water
Cook 45-60 minutes until all beans are tender
The different beans give different textures and flavors in one bowl
Kwati is filling, nutritious, and complex
It's the festival soup — prepared by families on Janai Purnima
dinner.description: Nepal's nine-bean festival soup — nine types of beans and lentils sprouted for 2-3 days (sprouting improves nutrition and digestibility), then simmered together with mustard oil, timur pepper, and spices. The nine beans represent the nine planets in Hindu-Buddhist cosmology. Made on Janai Purnima (August full moon). The mix of textures (each bean cooks differently) in a single pot is the Kwati experience.

snacks.name: Chatamari (Nepali Pizza)
instructions: Pour thin rice batter on hot pan
Add meat or crack egg on top
Add onion and chili
Cook until crispy underneath
snacks.description: Thin rice-flour crepe topped with meat or egg — Newari 'pizza'.

snacks.name: Chatamari (Newari Rice Crepe)
ingredients: Toppings: minced meat with egg and spices, OR sweet: coconut and sugar
instructions: Chatamari is the Newari pizza — rice flour crepe with toppings
One of the most important foods of the Newar people (Kathmandu Valley)
Mix rice flour with water and salt — a thin batter, thinner than pancake batter
Pour onto a hot, oiled flat pan
Add toppings immediately before the crepe sets
Savory: minced meat with egg, green onion, spices
Sweet: grated coconut, sugar, sometimes egg
Cook covered so the topping steams
The crepe is thin and slightly crispy at the edges
Chatamari is made at festivals and in Newari restaurants
The name 'Newari pizza' is a modern label — it predates pizza by centuries
Served at Indra Jatra and other Kathmandu Valley festivals
snacks.description: The Newar people's rice crepe — a thin rice flour batter poured onto a hot pan and immediately topped with minced meat and egg (savory) or coconut and sugar (sweet), cooked until the crepe is crispy at the edges and the topping is set. Called 'Newari pizza' (it predates pizza). Made for Indra Jatra and other Kathmandu Valley festivals — one of the most distinctive Newar foods.

snacks.name: Sukuti (Dried Meat Jerky)
instructions: Sukuti is Nepal's traditional dried meat — buffalo jerky
In Nepal, buffalo (not cow) is the traditional meat — Hindu communities don't eat beef
The meat is marinated with salt, spices, mustard oil
Hung and air-dried in the cold mountain air — or low oven
The drying preserves without refrigeration — important at altitude
The result: chewy, intensely flavored, spiced meat strips
Eaten as a snack, in curries, or as a side
The smoky, spiced, chewy buffalo sukuti is a Himalayan trekker snack
Newari festivals always include sukuti — it's a Newari celebration food
The mountain cold and dry air create the ideal sukuti conditions
Now made with chicken or goat — buffalo is traditional
snacks.description: Nepal's traditional dried buffalo jerky — buffalo meat (cows are sacred in Hindu Nepal; buffalo is the traditional red meat) marinated in mustard oil, salt, and spices, then air-dried in the mountain cold. The altitude and dry Himalayan air create ideal jerky conditions. Sukuti is a Newari festival staple and a Himalayan trekking snack. The chewy, intensely spiced strips are eaten alone or reconstituted in curries.

snacks.name: Tongba (Fermented Millet Hot Drink)
ingredients: Fermented millet (the tongba — a jarful of fermented millet)
A bamboo straw (tongba straw — filters out the grain)
instructions: Tongba is the traditional fermented drink of the Limbu people of eastern Nepal
Also popular in Darjeeling, Sikkim, and among the Rai people
The preparation: fermented millet packed into a wooden or bamboo container (also called tongba)
Hot water is poured over the fermented millet
Drunk through a bamboo straw with a filter — the straw strains out the grains
The hot water extracts the flavor — like a hot infusion
More hot water is added as you drink — the same grains can be steeped 3-4 times
The alcohol level is mild — like a warm, slightly alcoholic grain tea
Warming on cold mountain nights — traditionally drunk at altitude
The tongba container and bamboo straw are the vessel — they're part of the ritual
Tongba is the Himalayan warming drink — drunk while watching the mountains
snacks.description: The Limbu people's fermented millet drink — a jar of fermented millet stuffed with hot water and drunk through a filtered bamboo straw (the same straw that gives the drink its name). The hot water extracts warmth and gentle alcohol from the grain; the same millet can be steeped 3-4 times. Drunk in the mountains of eastern Nepal while watching the Himalayas at night. The tongba vessel and bamboo straw are inseparable from the ritual.

desserts.name: Juju Dhau (King Yogurt)
instructions: Heat milk, add sugar and cardamom
Pour into clay pot
Let set in warm place 6-8 hours
Serve chilled from clay pot
desserts.description: Bhaktapur's legendary creamy yogurt — set in clay pots.

desserts.name: Kheer (Nepali Rice Pudding)
instructions: Kheer is the universal South Asian milk rice pudding — but Nepal's version has its own character
Rice simmered in milk for 30-40 minutes — the milk thickens as the rice absorbs it
Long, slow cooking — stir regularly to prevent the bottom burning
Sugar added near the end
Cardamom is the principal spice
Saffron for the festival version — the yellow color is auspicious
The texture should be thick but pourable — not solid
Top with fried cashews, raisins, pistachios
Kheer is made for every Nepali festival — Dashain, Tihar, Teej, weddings
The smell of cardamom-kheer cooking means celebration in Nepal
Served on banana leaves at traditional feasts
desserts.description: Nepal's festival milk rice pudding — short-grain rice slowly simmered in full-fat milk until thick and creamy, with cardamom and saffron (the festival golden version). The long, slow cooking (30-40 minutes of stirring) develops the richness. Topped with fried cashews and pistachios. Made for every Nepali festival — Dashain, Tihar, weddings. The cardamom smell from the kitchen announces that something special is being prepared.

desserts.name: Juju Dhau (King Yoghurt)
ingredients: Full-fat buffalo milk (higher fat than cow milk — essential)
A small amount of active yoghurt culture (from previous batch)
Earthenware pots (the terra cotta absorbs excess moisture — essential for the texture)
instructions: Juju Dhau means 'king yoghurt' in Newari — and it lives up to the name
Made only in Bhaktapur (a city in Kathmandu Valley) — the terra cotta pots are specific to Bhaktapur
The earthenware pot absorbs excess moisture — creates a thicker, creamier yoghurt than metal or glass
Buffalo milk is essential — higher fat content than cow milk
Heat buffalo milk until hot, cool to 40-45°C
Add a small amount of active culture
Pour into the earthenware pot
Incubate 6-8 hours in a warm place (or overnight)
The yoghurt should be thick, creamy, slightly sweet — rich
Bhaktapur's Juju Dhau is famous across Nepal — people travel to Bhaktapur to buy it
Sold in the earthenware pot — the pot is part of the purchase
Served at weddings and festivals
desserts.description: Nepal's 'king yoghurt' — made exclusively in Bhaktapur (Kathmandu Valley) in specific earthenware pots that absorb moisture, creating a texture impossible to replicate in metal or glass. Buffalo milk (higher fat than cow) is essential. The result: thick, creamy, slightly sweet yoghurt that is Nepal's most prized dairy product. People travel to Bhaktapur specifically to buy Juju Dhau. Served at weddings.

drinks.name: Chiya (Nepali Tea)
instructions: Boil water with ginger and cardamom
Add tea and milk
Simmer 5 min
Strain, sweeten
drinks.description: Spiced milk tea — Nepal runs on this.

drinks.name: Tongba (Millet Beer)
instructions: Pack fermented millet in bamboo vessel
Pour hot water over
Wait 5 minutes
Sip through bamboo straw
Refill with hot water multiple times
drinks.description: Hot millet beer sipped through a straw — Himalayan mountain tradition.

drinks.name: Masala Tea / Nepali Chiya
instructions: Nepali chiya (tea) is the foundation of Nepali social life
Made by boiling the spices first — ginger and cardamom in water
Add tea — a strong black tea (Ilam tea from eastern Nepal is prestigious)
Add milk — half and half with water is common
Simmer 5 minutes — the tea and milk merge
Add sugar to taste
The spices are Nepali: ginger is generous, cardamom is forward
Ilam district (eastern Nepal, near Darjeeling) produces excellent Nepali tea
Less well-known internationally than Darjeeling but from the same Himalayan tea belt
Chiya is drunk in the morning, after lunch, during rest, and as hospitality
Refusing tea in Nepal is impolite — it is offered at every home visit
The street chiya wallah (tea seller) is a fixture of every Nepali town
drinks.description: Nepal's foundational social drink — strong black tea (ideally Ilam tea from eastern Nepal's Himalayan tea belt, neighboring Darjeeling) boiled with ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, and milk. Refusing tea in Nepal is impolite: it is offered at every home, business, and rest stop. The street chiya wallah is a fixture of every Nepali town. Ilam tea is Nepal's prestige tea, less known internationally than Darjeeling but from the same mountain range.
